text: PRE-REGISTERED (plan 5a62fdf6d614), audit CONFIRMATORY. 6 candidates co-folded with their declared receptors, each against 3 composition-matched shuffles. NOT ONE CANDIDATE beat its own null: fraction_beating_null = 0.0. Mean native ipTM 0.405 versus mean decoy 0.4113 — the designed sequences score very slightly WORSE than random rearrangements of their own amino acids (-0.0062). H1 and H2 FALSIFIED, H3 CONFIRMED with 5 of 6 in the band where study #7 measured 0 of 4 interfaces correct.

THIS NEGATIVE IS INTERPRETABLE, which is the whole reason study #7 ran first. The gate was OPEN: #7 recovered 7 of 8 memorisable peptide interfaces and showed ipTM tracks DockQ at rho 0.847 with zero false negatives below 0.6. So the pipeline has demonstrated sensitivity on this exact modality, and a low score here is evidence about the candidate rather than about the method. Without that gate the same numbers would have been indistinguishable from method failure.

WHY THE COMPOSITION NULL WAS NECESSARY, demonstrated twice. A random shuffle of PfcACh-PAM-P1 scored ipTM 0.8365 against CHRNA7 — inside the confident band, above every native — and a shuffle of BasalAChE-Abeta-B4 scored 0.7418 against AChE. Reported without a null, either would have read as a hit. These candidates are Arg/Trp-rich cationic amphipathic peptides, the class most prone to scoring on composition alone, so an absolute ipTM threshold would have measured composition rather than design.

INTERNAL CONSISTENCY CHECK PASSED, unplanned. HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 and BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1 returned byte-identical ipTM (0.3402) and identical decoy values, because they are one of the duplicate sequence pairs the data gate flagged. Identical inputs producing identical outputs confirms both that the pipeline is deterministic at fixed seed and that the duplicate-sequence finding was real: the platform listed them as two distinct therapeutics against different targets.

SCOPE LIMIT, registered in advance. Three decoys give a minimum empirical p of 0.25, so no individual candidate could reach significance; the design tests the SET and per-candidate p values are descriptive. A negative bounds what THIS pipeline detects at THIS configuration, not what the molecules do in a cell. Only 6 of 25 candidates were screened — those whose receptor is in the registry AND extracellular.

task: retract the study-#9 gate reading falsified by study #12

text: RETRACTION. Two earlier ledger claims -- clm_382ac4400a7b562c (study-candidate-screen) and clm_794767aa2f5699b2 (study-peptide-interface) -- read study #7's open gate as licensing 'a low score here is evidence about the candidate rather than about the method'. Study #12, interface-null-positive-control-v1, falsified that reading: 16 deposited X-ray complexes, all established binders, each folded against ten uniform random permutations of its own peptide under #7's settings, and only 4 of 16 beat all ten of their own permutations against a pre-registered threshold of 5 (H2 FALSIFIED, P(X>=4) = 0.0511 under Bin(16, 1/11)). Losing the composition-matched comparison is therefore the normal behaviour of a demonstrated binder on this instrument, and a low score in #9 is not evidence about the candidate in the way those claims asserted. The per-candidate reading of the composition-matched null is withdrawn. #7's 7-of-8 recovery and #12's aggregate separation (+0.0895 ipTM, Holm p = 0.0148, 13 of 16 positive) both stand, and license a verdict on a batch of native-versus-shuffle pairs only. Corrected in README.md (Slate #7 gate paragraph), platform/studies/candidate_screen.py and data/study_candidate_screen.json analysis.interpretation_key.
